summary: Remark42 is a privacy-focused, self-hosted commenting engine designed to be embedded directly into static sites, blogs, and articles. It provides a lightweight backend and frontend widget for managing reader discussions without relying on third-party tracking networks. Written in Go and distributed under the MIT license, it offers a transparent alternative to hosted commenting services.
goodFor: Self-hosters and site owners who want to offer reader discussions on static blogs or websites while strictly avoiding user tracking and third-party data collection.
watchOut: Adoption requires managing your own backend instance and handling comment moderation infrastructure, which adds an ongoing operational overhead compared to turnkey hosted alternatives.
deployNotes: As a containerised Go application, it typically requires persistent storage volumes for comment data and sits behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
